findings.title: Appended devhash functions are called before their definition; ptxas rejects that, and no test before S8 assembles a routed module
findings.plan_section: D1; S6 code; S0 item 2
findings.problem: The routing pass "appends them (`.func`, not `.visible`) to the module and calls them directly", but the call sites are in probe functions that sit earlier in the module. PTX needs a prototype before a call. Literal appending therefore fails at ptxas. S6's tests compare text only. S3's module is composed by hand. S0 item 2 appends the functions without calling them. So the first module that would fail to assemble is S8's llama.cpp run.
findings.evidence: Plan line 27: "appends them (`.func`, not `.visible`) to the module and calls them directly". CPU compile in /tmp/claude-2002/devhash-plan-review/coverage/callfirst.ptx: kernel k_call calls `heavy`, which is defined after it with no prototype. ptxas -arch=sm_87: "error : Call to 'heavy' requires call prototype" / "Unknown symbol 'heavy'" / "ptxas fatal : Ptx assembly aborted due to errors".
findings.suggested_change: State where the functions go: forward `.func` declarations before the first probe function, or the definitions inserted after the trampoline and before the probes. Add an S6 test that runs ptxas (sm_87) on a routed module containing an inline 1533 lookup that falls back to `devhash_lookup` and a rewritten update that calls `devhash_insert`. Mutation: append after the probes with no declaration; ptxas must fail.

findings.title: S0 item 2's rules cannot fail: ptxas drops uncalled functions and leaves kernels unchanged
findings.plan_section: S0 item 2; section 3 row 'new PTX forms, register and occupancy effect'
findings.problem: S0 appends devhash.cu to the 11-26 by-value modules. Those modules hold 1531 probes, so nothing calls the hash functions. ptxas then emits no SASS for them and leaves every kernel's registers unchanged. Both rules ("SASS shows the .STRONG.GPU forms and MEMBAR/ERRBAR"; "no probed kernel loses warps per SM") hold whatever the functions contain. Code-map risk 1.R5 ("the register and occupancy effect of a noinline helper that now contains a loop") is therefore unhandled. DESIGN's C3 rule ("a kernel that gains registers or loses warps per SM with the inline path keeps the helper call") also loses its register half and its consequence.
findings.evidence:
Compile A/B in /tmp/claude-2002/devhash-plan-review/coverage/:
- base.ptx: k_nocall "Used 8 registers".
- With an uncalled `.func heavy` appended (appended.ptx), and also with `.visible .func` (appended_vis.ptx): k_nocall still "Used 8 registers", and `cuobjdump -sass` lists only "Function : k_nocall" (heavy is dropped).
- regs.ptx: the kernel that calls heavy (k_call) uses 24 registers and 192 bytes of stack.
Plan line 176: "no probed kernel loses warps per SM against the same build without the functions". DESIGN.md:172.
findings.suggested_change: Make S0 item 2 compile modules in which probes actually call `devhash_insert`/`devhash_lookup`: hand-route the hash tool's probe the way C2's `hcall` was. Compare registers and warps per SM against the same probes on 1531. Restore DESIGN's rule (gains registers or loses warps -> keep the helper call / report). Re-run it on the final devhash_ptx.h in S8.

findings.title: D1 and S6 disagree on base 0, and inlining NULL drops the reason 1531 keeps the trampoline call
findings.plan_section: D1; S6 'Base 0'; S6 mirror of :135
findings.problem: D1 sends calls with "no device copy at patch time" to the trampoline, while S6 says "Base 0: NULL and -1 inline". 1531 deliberately keeps the trampoline call at base 0 so that a copy made later (after an owner exits) is still found through the run-time map_info; an inlined NULL in a cached image would never find it. Under the plan, both paths return NULL/-1 for good: the inline form, and D1's trampoline branches, which are unconditional. So a D11 takeover never reaches modules patched while another process owned the map. S6 also says it "mirrors" :135, which asserts the opposite behaviour.
findings.evidence: Plan line 31: trampoline branches "serve calls the pass does not rewrite (a non-constant fd, or no device copy at patch time)". Plan line 364: "**Base 0:** NULL and -1 inline." test_sum_map_routing.cpp:135-139: "a copy made later (after an owner exits) is then still found: the trampoline reads the run-time map_info, a cached patched image would keep an inlined NULL". nv_thread_local_routing.cpp:1166-1168, same reason.
findings.suggested_change: Pick one rule and write it in both D1 and S6. Either keep the trampoline call at base 0 and say that takeover reaches only modules patched afterwards (README), or have the trampoline branch read map_info at run time. Replace "mirror of :135" with the 1533 expectation, and add a test that pins it.

findings.title: The trampoline's 1533 branches have no test, so falling through to host_call goes unseen
findings.plan_section: D1; S3 'flags and delete'; section 3 row 'no device copy must not fall through'
findings.problem: Any map type without its own branch reaches host_call in all three helpers. The only no-copy test in the plan, S3's "With no copy (base 0): -1 and NULL", runs the devhash functions, which per D1 never receive base 0. The paths that are taken (non-constant fd and base 0, both through the trampoline per D1) are never executed. Mutation: drop the 1533 branch from `_bpf_helper_ext_0001/0002/0003`. Lookups then become host calls, and no test fails. Code-map risk 1.R4 and test 1.T0 are not covered.
findings.evidence: default_trampoline.cu:342, :436, :462: `HelperCallResponse resp = host_call(` after the typed branches. Plan line 292: "With no copy (base 0): -1 and NULL" under S3, whose tests run "through `devhash_ptx.h` in a module with test kernels" (line 282). test_cuda_host_call.cpp:461-500 (test_module wraps TEST_KERNELS_PTX with the real trampoline) and :592-604 (counting_host counts any host call).
findings.suggested_change: Add a GPU test in test_cuda_host_call.cpp: a 1533 map_info, with extra_buffer both 0 and non-zero, and kernels calling helpers 1/2/3 through the real trampoline. Expect NULL, -1 and -22, with counting_host.served == 0. Mutation: remove the 1533 branch, so served > 0.

findings.title: The S6 gate test cannot see 1533 missing from the gate
findings.plan_section: S6 tests 'a module whose only GPU-model map is 1533 is routed'; section 3 row 'no 1533 in the pass gate'
findings.problem: The routing tests call route_thread_local_maps directly with hand-made descriptors. The gate (`if (descs.empty() && sums.empty() && !device_arrays) return ptx;`) sits in nv_attach_impl::route_thread_local_maps_of_module, which builds the descriptors from map_basic_info, and no test calls it. A [hash-map-routing] case written like the 1531 ones passes even when 1533 is left out of the gate (code-map risk 0.R5).
findings.evidence: test_sum_map_routing.cpp:69-73: `route()` returns `route_thread_local_maps(ptx, { K }, {}, 0, &st, s)`. nv_attach_impl.cpp:1042-1043: the gate inside route_thread_local_maps_of_module. `grep route_thread_local_maps_of_module attach/ runtime/unit-test` finds only its declaration (nv_attach_impl.hpp:214) and its definition.
findings.suggested_change: Test the gate through route_thread_local_maps_of_module (or a small free function factored out of it) with a map_basic_info whose only enabled GPU-model map is 1533. Mutation: 1533 left out of the gate, so the PTX comes back unchanged.

findings.title: No test fails if the insert's release or the snapshot's acquire is removed
findings.plan_section: S0 items 2-3; S3 controls; S5; S8 'Every unit test of S1-S6 runs once more'
findings.problem:
Code-map test 1.T4 asks for C4's "publish without release" control against the built bodies. The plan's controls are 1/2/5/6 only.
- C5's run h reader is too slow to see the publish.
- In C6, dropping only one side (variants B and C) gave 0 weak outcomes, so S0 item 3's "0 weak" rule cannot tell `ld.acquire` from no acquire.
- S0's SASS check applies to "S3's first draft", and S8 re-runs only S1-S6's unit tests.
So `st.relaxed` in devhash_insert's publish, or an `ld.relaxed` header load in the hash snapshot, would pass every test in the plan.
findings.evidence: README.md:48: "the reader is too slow to test the publish". README.md:89-90: variants B and C, 0 weak. Plan line 171: "`devhash.cu`, the C5 bodies ported** (S3's first draft)". Plan line 429: "Every unit test of S1-S6 runs once more on the final build." code-map 1.T4: "a publish without release, and the claim protocol without the count reservation".
findings.suggested_change: Add a unit test that parses the final devhash_ptx.h and the hash snapshot PTX: the publish store must be `st.release.gpu.global.b64`, the snapshot's header load the S0-decided acquire form, and the CAS/count/adds must have the stated qualifiers. Optionally also check ptxas SASS for MEMBAR before STG.STRONG.GPU. Mutation: replace `.release` with `.relaxed`, and the test fails. Run it again in S8.

findings.title: C5's checker cannot be ported through D6's return codes; diagnostic counters and run g's build are missing
findings.plan_section: S3 tests; D5; D6; S1 layout
findings.problem:
RULES-round2 needs to know, thread by thread, whether an EEXIST was unstable ("EEXIST not counted unstable > 0 implies the key is live"; "EEXIST (not unstable) followed by NULL = 0"). D6 returns -17 for both kinds, so a test kernel calling devhash_insert cannot apply these rules. In run g they would fire falsely (73,485 unstable-then-NULL).

The checker also reads protocol counters that the S1 layout and the D5 counters do not have: C_KEY_CHANGED, C_ROW_OVERFLOW and C_REFUSED_PUBLISHED. Control 6 needs C_NEXT_ROW and the give-back counter.

Run g was a separate build with wait bound 0 (`c5_proto_nowait`), but devhash_ptx.h is checked in with 100,000 ns, and the plan names fault builds only.
findings.evidence: Plan line 60: "-17 (EEXIST, including unstable)". RULES-round2.md:69-70. c5.cu:1058-1063 (then_null split on OC_EEXIST_UNSTABLE), :1069-1078, :1122-1124, :1028-1032. c5-device-part.cu:341-403 (FAULT 6 uses C_NEXT_ROW and C_GIVEBACK). Plan lines 190-192: control words "magic, max_entries, S, R, shards, count, reserved". run_rules.sh: `run g0-nowait-64k-128 $B/c5_proto_nowait`.
findings.suggested_change: Give the test builds an outcome channel. For example, under BPFTIME_DEVHASH_TEST, an out-parameter or per-thread byte with C5's OC_* codes and C5's diagnostic counters in a test-only region. Add a wait-bound macro so the test builds run g. Or state which RULES-round2 checks are dropped and why.

findings.title: The opaque test can miss the port's main bug unless K = 0
findings.plan_section: D4; S3 'opaque' test; D10 CPU walk
findings.problem: C5 compares the key field first and then decides on the state. On a key match that is not live, lookup returns NULL and insert waits as if the slot were claiming. An opaque header has key field 0 ("occupied with no key"). A port that adds "walk past opaque" but keeps C5's order therefore stops at, or waits 100 us on, every opaque slot when K = 0. The S3 opaque test ("K is inserted past them") sees this only if K happens to be 0, and the plan does not say so. Key 0 is common (SM 0, bin 0, block 0). The CPU mirror walk (D10) has the same exposure, because repair writes opaque slots there.
findings.evidence: c5-device-part.cu:250-252 (`if ((u32)(h >> 32) == K) { if (st != ST_LIVE) return 0;`) and :414-422 (key match, not live or refused, so it waits). Plan lines 48-51: "New: 4 opaque, meaning occupied with no key ... matches K only when the state is 1, 2 or 3". Plan lines 290-291.
findings.suggested_change: Require K = 0 (and one other K) in the S3 opaque test and in the S2 mirror test, with opaque slots on the probe path. Mutation: key-first compare as in C5; lookup must not return NULL early, and insert must not end unstable.

findings.title: The S2 mirror rules cannot see the 'no repair' and 'no pass B' mutations
findings.plan_section: S2 mirror test
findings.problem: The rules are "once a reader has found a key live, it finds it on every later lookup" and "a found value is never below the value staged". Without repair, or with headers stored in one ascending pass, a reader only misses a newly delivered key until the gap slot is filled. Mirror slots never return to empty, so a key once found is never lost, and values are untouched. Neither mutation can violate the stated rules. Code-map test 3.T3 (every key that get_next_key returns, or that is live in the mirror, is found by lookup) is the check that sees them, and it is not in the plan.
findings.evidence: Plan lines 252-255: "Rules: once a reader has found a key live, it finds it on every later lookup ... Mutations that must fail: no repair; headers stored in one pass (no pass B)". Plan line 101: "A mirror slot never goes back to empty". code-map 3.T3: "check that every key get_next_key returns is found by lookup".
findings.suggested_change: Add the rule: a reader that reads `mhdr[j]` live K directly (acquire), or gets K from get_next_key, must then find K by lookup. Include stagings where K's home is near S-1 and K is at a low slot, so that one ascending pass is caught.

findings.title: The 'slot allowed back to empty' mutation needs stagings a faithful device model never produces
findings.plan_section: S2 mirror test; D10
findings.problem: D10 argues that a slot repaired to opaque is delivered non-empty in every later staging, because the device header is monotone and the next snapshot is stream-ordered after the acquire. Stagings "made from a host model of the device directory" then never stage empty over a non-empty mirror slot. With faithful input, the mutation that lets a slot return to empty changes nothing and cannot fail.
findings.evidence: Plan lines 101-102 and 111-113 (the argument); lines 249-250 ("synthetic stagings, made from a host model of the device directory"); line 255 ("a slot allowed back to empty").
findings.suggested_change: Say that the generator also emits stagings that re-show a repaired slot as empty: a defensive input that D10's argument excludes. Or drop that mutation and record the rule as unchecked.

findings.title: The inline hit path's state check, row decode and addresses run only as text
findings.plan_section: S6 inline hit path; section 3 row 'layout copies disagree'
findings.evidence: Plan lines 354-361 (the inline path) and 378-379 ("the emitted hash equals `home_slot` (the text is run on the GPU ...)"). code-map 1.R3: "A mismatch gives silent misses or a second slot for one key ... test that the copies agree."
findings.suggested_change: Run the emitted inline lookup on the GPU over a directory seeded with the layout header. Cases: live at home, row < R and row >= R, plus claiming, refused and opaque at home. Its pointer or NULL must equal devhash_lookup's for each thread. Mutations: no state check; row >= R treated as sharded.

findings.title: C5 run d (keys inserted beforehand) is dropped, so prefilled keys never meet GPU inserts and adds
findings.plan_section: S3 runs; S4 tests
findings.problem: S3 ports runs a, b, c, e, g and h. Run d, where 16 keys are placed by the host as the agent's copy and then inserted with NOEXIST and added to by the GPU, is not ported. S4 only checks that prefilled keys sit at the image's slots. No test checks that a seeded key gets EEXIST and never a second slot from a GPU insert, or that its delivered value equals the seeded value plus the adds. DESIGN's C4 requires "Sums are checked for keys inserted beforehand".
findings.evidence: Plan line 282: "C5's runs a, b, c, e, g and h". RULES-round2.md:55: "| d | 64 | 128 | 16 keys inserted beforehand | 1 + 200 |". c5.cu:854-871 (host prefill), :1083 (PREFILL_V in the expected sum). DESIGN.md:174. Plan line 312: "Prefilled keys are at the image's slots on the device".
findings.suggested_change: Port run d with the image from seal_and_build_image() (the S2 function) in place of C5's host prefill. Or extend S5's end-to-end test: CPU prefill, copy, then GPU NOEXIST inserts and adds on those keys, then delivery. Expect one slot per key and delivered = seeded + adds - counted EEXIST.

findings.title: The seal-race mutation is caught only with timing luck
findings.plan_section: S2 seal race
findings.problem: With 'writer skips INFLIGHT', a key is lost only when its insert completes after the sealer's iteration has passed its bucket, within the few hundred ns between the writer's PHASE load and its insert. The plan names one seal, no repetition count and no hook to hold a writer inside that window. Whether the test fails under its own mutation depends on timing.
findings.evidence: Plan lines 242-244: "8 writer threads insert distinct keys while the sealer seals. Every key is in the image or its writer got EPERM. Mutation that must fail: the writer skips INFLIGHT." D8 (lines 72-75).
findings.suggested_change: Add a test hook that parks a writer after its PHASE load (or after INFLIGHT++) until the sealer has stored PHASE = 1. Or name a repetition count, many seals on fresh maps, shown to fail under the mutation.

findings.title: The SIGKILL seal test expects 'later CPU updates work', which fails if the kill lands under the table's stripe lock
findings.plan_section: S2 seal race (SIGKILL); D8
findings.problem: Killed "inside an update", a writer holds the CPU table's stripe lock. CLAUDE.md documents that later writers of that stripe, and next_key reaching it, then hang. The test's expected outcome holds only if the kill lands between INFLIGHT++ and the lock, or after unlock and before fetch_sub, and the plan names no hook to place it there. INFLIGHT also stays at 1 for good, so every later seal times out and the map never gets a device copy. That consequence is in no test and not in the S7 README list.
findings.evidence: Plan lines 245-246: "a writer process forked and SIGKILLed inside an update (INFLIGHT left at 1): the seal times out, PHASE returns to 0, and later CPU updates work." CLAUDE.md:976-978: "A process killed inside a writer leaves its stripe locked (writers of that stripe and `next_key` calls reaching it hang, lookups do not)". Plan lines 78-79 (fails closed on timeout).
findings.suggested_change: Place the kill with a hook outside the table's lock (after INFLIGHT++, before the operation), and test a second seal attempt (it times out again). Add to the README that a writer dying mid-update leaves the map CPU-only for the life of the segment, and its stripe locked if it died inside the table.

findings.title: An owner that dies before PHASE = 2 is not handled: takeover seeds from an empty mirror
findings.plan_section: D11; S4 steps 1-7 and 'Takeover uses takeover_image()'
findings.problem: S4 takes ownership first (step 1) and stores PHASE = 2 last (step 7). If the owner dies in between, a new process sees a dead OWNER_PID and takes the takeover path. That path seeds from the mirror, which is still empty, while the prefill is in the CPU table, so every prefilled key is lost. PHASE may also stay 1, so CPU writes get EPERM. The plan does not say that takeover chooses by PHASE, and the only takeover test starts "after one delivery" (phase 2). Code-map risk 2.R3 (takeover drops keys) is handled only for phase 2.
findings.evidence: Plan lines 297-305 (order: owner CAS ... PHASE = 2) and line 306: "Takeover uses `takeover_image()`." Lines 118-119: "seeds the fresh block from the mirror". Line 315: "a forked owner exits after one delivery".
findings.suggested_change: State the rule: with a dead owner and PHASE != 2, seal again from the CPU table; with PHASE 2, use takeover_image. Add S4 tests that kill the owner after the CAS and after the seal (test hooks). Prefilled keys must survive, and PHASE must end at 2.

findings.title: No test reaches full_directory() with the count below max_entries, which D11 seeding can produce
findings.plan_section: D11; S3 termination test; R2 #2
findings.problem: C5's full_directory() waits for count >= max_entries and otherwise times out into an unstable E2BIG. D11 resets count to L (delivered live slots) and turns every other non-empty slot opaque. If the last delivery showed some slots still claiming, a directory filled with refused slots stays full while count = L < max_entries. Every new insert then spends the whole 100 us wait and returns unstable E2BIG, for good. This is the deterministic trigger of R2 #2, and no test covers it. The termination test reaches the full directory only with count >= max. Mutations a 'fulldir timeout not counted unstable' and an unbounded full-directory wait both pass.
findings.evidence: c5-device-part.cu:319-336 (`if (ld_acquire(...C_BOUND) >= c.max_entries) ... if (total >= WAIT_BOUND_NS) { ... C_FULLDIR_UNSTABLE`). Plan lines 120-122: "every other non-empty slot (claiming, refused, opaque) becomes opaque; count = L". README.md:116 (R2 #2). Plan lines 287-289 (termination at max 48, one key per thread).
findings.suggested_change: Add an S3 case: a seeded directory with no empty slot and count < max_entries. An insert of a new key returns -7, the unstable-E2BIG counter rises, and the kernel ends. Mutation: an unbounded wait, so the watchdog fires. Then decide whether D11 should set count to max_entries when the seeded directory is full, and document the case.

findings.title: The delete count in D5 is unreachable, and S3 tests a delete function the plan does not build
findings.plan_section: D5; D1; D6; S3 'flags and delete'; S6 'Constant-fd delete'
findings.problem:
D5 counts "bad operation (other flags, delete)", and S3 tests "flags and delete: -22 and counted". But the plan defines only `devhash_lookup` and `devhash_insert`, and no path counts a delete:
- a constant-fd delete becomes "-22 inline" in S6, with no counter add;
- a non-constant-fd delete hits the trampoline, which D1 keeps sm_61-legal ("no 64-bit `atom`"), so it cannot count either.
The S3 test has no code to run, and the delete part of the counter is always 0.
findings.evidence: Plan line 55: "bad operation (other flags, delete)". Line 25: "the device functions (`devhash_lookup`, `devhash_insert`)". Lines 21 and 29-30: trampoline "no 64-bit `atom`" ... "delete -EINVAL". Line 292: "**flags and delete:** -22 and counted". Line 363: "**Constant-fd delete:** -22 inline."
findings.suggested_change: Either emit a sharded `red` on the bad-operation counter in S6's inline delete (and say the trampoline delete is uncounted), or drop deletes from D5. Then make the S3/S6 test match the code that exists, with a mutation: no count, and the test fails.

findings.title: ASan cannot see the pin-list mutation, and the 'close while delivering' test is never defined
findings.plan_section: S4 tests (pin list mutation); section 3 row 'pin list (use after free)'
findings.problem: Map objects are constructed and destroyed inside the boost managed shared-memory segment, not with malloc/free. ASan does not track those blocks, so a delivery writing into a destroyed 1533 object gives no ASan report. In addition, the "close while delivering" test that the mutation names appears nowhere in S4's test list. Code-map test 3.T7 is unhandled.
findings.evidence: map_handler.cpp:1623-1626 (`memory.construct<nv_gpu_device_array_map_impl>(...anonymous_instance)`), :1789-1792 (`memory.destroy_ptr(...)`), :1921-1941 (the pin: `inc_map_refcount()` once per process). Plan lines 319-320: "Mutation that must fail: 1533 left out of the pin list, so the "close while delivering" test sees a freed object (run under ASan)."
findings.suggested_change: Define the test: close the tool's fd and drop the last reference while the delivery runs. Check the map's refcount (or that map_free was not called) through a test hook, or poison the freed shm block, instead of relying on ASan. Mutation: 1533 left out of the pin list, so the refcount reaches zero or map_free runs.

findings.title: S5's sync-coverage checks are empty in a unit test: app syncs come only from the agent's hooks, and AT_SYNC is read once per process
findings.plan_section: S5 end-to-end test
findings.problem: "SYNCS_COVERED = app syncs" is checked against app_sync_count, which only the agent's Frida sync hooks increment; they also fire the at-sync listener. A test that calls cudaDeviceSynchronize without the agent leaves the count at 0, so the check passes trivially and at-sync delivery never runs. "Repeat with BPFTIME_GPU_DELIVERY_AT_SYNC=1" in the same process has no effect either: deliver_at_sync() caches the variable in a function-local static on first use.
findings.evidence: nv_attach_impl_frida_setup.cpp:625-633 (`launch_activity().note_app_sync()` in the cuStreamSynchronize hook). probed_launch_activity.hpp:68-77 (note_app_sync increments and calls the listener). nv_gpu_model_maps.cpp:269-275 (`static const bool on = [] { const char *v = getenv("BPFTIME_GPU_DELIVERY_AT_SYNC"); ...}();`). Plan lines 341-344.
findings.suggested_change: In the test, call `attach::launch_activity().note_app_sync()` after each of the test's own synchronizes, and require SYNCS_COVERED to equal a non-zero count. Run the AT_SYNC variant in a re-exec'd child with the variable set (the pattern in test_cuda_no_device.cpp:93-104). Mutation: the delivery does not record syncs, and the test fails.

findings.title: S4/S5 GPU tests in one test binary collide with process-wide delivery state and the per-address copy cache
findings.plan_section: S4 and S5 tests
findings.evidence: nv_gpu_model_maps.cpp:256 (`static auto *s = new delivery_state();`), :651 (`s.maps.push_back(m);`, with no erase anywhere), :698-702 (`static std::vector<made_copy> made; ... if (mc.map == this) return mc.device;`). test_cuda_host_call.cpp:651-663 (agent_segment destroys and removes the segment per test). code-map 4.T5: "no unit test names 1531 or 1532".
findings.suggested_change: Run each S4/S5 GPU test that registers a delivery or takes ownership in its own re-exec'd child (test_cuda_no_device.cpp:93-104 pattern), or add a test-only reset of the delivery state and the copy cache. State the choice in the plan.

findings.title: Step order does not fit the tests: S4's takeover and lifetime tests need S5's delivery, S6 needs S3, and the forked owner uses CUDA
findings.plan_section: Section 2 'Order'; S4 tests; S6 tests
findings.problem:
The plan says "Each step builds and its tests pass before the next one that depends on it. Order: ... then S4, S5". But:
- S4's takeover test needs "a forked owner [that] exits after one delivery", and its pin-list mutation needs "close while delivering". Delivery (snapshot, apply_delivery into the mirror) is built in S5.
- S6's hash-equality test runs "in S3's test module", while S3 and S6 are listed as "in any order".
- A child forked after the parent has initialized CUDA cannot use CUDA. The repository's multi-process CUDA test re-execs itself for that reason.
findings.evidence: Plan line 165 (order), lines 315-316 (takeover after one delivery), line 319 (close while delivering), lines 325-333 (delivery built in S5), lines 378-379 ("run on the GPU in S3's test module"). test_cuda_no_device.cpp:93-104 (fork, then `execl("/proc/self/exe", ...)`).
findings.suggested_change: Move S4's takeover and lifetime tests to S5, or order S5 before those tests. Order S3 before S6. Write the owner as a re-exec'd child.

findings.title: Two hash maps can bind the same companion: the name rule refuses duplicate companions only
findings.plan_section: D12; S4 companion test
findings.problem: The companion name is the hash map's name cut to 12 bytes plus "_st". Two hash maps whose names share their first 12 bytes look up the same companion name. If the tool declared one companion, each finds exactly one match and both bind it, so two deliveries write their status words into one array. D12 refuses only the case of two companion candidates. Code-map risk 2.R6 ("a suffix rule can collide") is handled in one direction only. findings.title: S4/S5 GPU tests share process-wide delivery state that is never reset, and plain fork inherits it
findings.plan_section: S4 tests (second process, takeover, failure, companion, ASan); S5 tests (hand-built block, end to end, AT_SYNC repeat, failure isolation)
findings.problem: No unit test registers a map for delivery today, and these would be the first. The delivery state lives for the whole process. Once a test registers a map, the drain thread and the atexit handler keep delivering into that map object after the test's agent_segment has destroyed and removed its segment. The per-process `made` cache is keyed by object address, so a later test's map at the same address gets the old device pointer, without allocation or seeding. `deliver_at_sync()` reads BPFTIME_GPU_DELIVERY_AT_SYNC once into a static, so "Repeat with BPFTIME_GPU_DELIVERY_AT_SYNC=1" cannot run in the same process. A plain fork() child inherits `made`: after the parent's copy exists, "a second process gets 0" returns the parent's device pointer instead. A CUDA-using child ("a forked owner exits after one delivery") also inherits the parent's CUDA state. The repo's CUDA tests use fork plus exec for children.
findings.evidence: nv_gpu_model_maps.cpp:256 `static auto *s = new delivery_state();`, never destroyed. The header (:153-158) has no unregister. cpp:660-661 `atexit(final_delivery_at_exit); s.thread = std::thread(drain_loop);`. cpp:698-702 `static std::vector<made_copy> made; for (auto &mc : made) if (mc.map == this) return mc.device;`, with no pid check. cpp:271 `static const bool on = [] { getenv("BPFTIME_GPU_DELIVERY_AT_SYNC") ...`. test_cuda_host_call.cpp:660 ~agent_segment destroys and removes the segment. test_cuda_no_device.cpp:93-104 forks, then `execl("/proc/self/exe", ..., "[.cuda-no-device-child]")`.
findings.suggested_change: Run each S4/S5 GPU case that registers a delivery in its own exec'd child of the test binary, using a hidden test tag as [.cuda-no-device-child] does. Do the same for the owner child and the second process. Alternatively, add a test-only reset that stops the drain thread, clears `maps` and `made`, and unregisters the atexit work, and say which cases use it.

findings.title: S5 end to end: the test binary counts no app syncs, and deliver_now(false) skips maps that are not due
findings.plan_section: S5 tests, end to end ("then sync, then deliver_now ... SYNCS_COVERED = app syncs. Repeat with BPFTIME_GPU_DELIVERY_AT_SYNC=1")
findings.problem: App syncs are counted only by the agent's frida hooks, which only agent.cpp creates. In bpftime_runtime_tests a cuCtxSynchronize is not counted, so SYNCS_COVERED == app syncs is 0 == 0 and checks nothing. The AT_SYNC variant never delivers, because at-sync delivery runs only from the sync listener that note_app_sync() calls. Also, deliver_now(false) runs the drain rule: a map is skipped while it is not due, and after registration it is not due for busy_ns (20 ms) unless an uncovered sync makes it due. Without a counted sync, a deliver_now right after the kernel may deliver nothing.
findings.evidence: agent.cpp:1136 is the only `make_unique<attach::nv_attach_impl>`. note_app_sync is called only in nv_attach_impl_frida_setup.cpp:626-675 (the sync hooks), and grep finds no call under runtime/unit-test. on_app_sync is at nv_gpu_model_maps.cpp:278-289. The due test is cpp:390 `if (!at_exit && due > t0) { ... continue; }`. cpp:631 sets `m.next_due_ns = now_ns() + m.busy_ns`.
findings.suggested_change: In the test, call attach::launch_activity().note_app_sync() after each synchronize. Then assert that SYNCS_COVERED equals the number of note_app_sync calls. Assert that deliver_now returned at least 1 delivered map, or wait for the sync gap first. Run the AT_SYNC repeat in a separate exec'd process (see buildability-5).

findings.title: The SIGKILL seal test needs a named hook, and "later CPU updates work" fails if the kill lands inside the stripe lock

findings.title: D9's seal iteration takes the stripe locks D8 claims to avoid, so the seal can hang with no bound

The sealer then passes its 1 s wait and blocks forever in the iteration, inside get_gpu_mem_buffer on the application thread at its first CUDA link.
findings.evidence: bpftime_hash_map.hpp:784-822 next_key calls bpftime_spin_lock(&st.lock) per stripe. fix_hash_map.hpp declares map_get_next_key and no lock-free walk. CLAUDE.md:977-978: "a tool killed inside `next_key` is such a holder too". Plan D8 counts only "A CPU writer does INFLIGHT.fetch_add(1)".

findings.title: The S2 mirror test rules cannot catch the "no repair" and "no pass B" mutations
findings.plan_section: S2 tests, mirror (rules: "once a reader has found a key live, it finds it on every later lookup; a found value is never below the value staged")
findings.problem: Without repair, or with headers stored in one pass, a delivered gap makes a reader's walk stop at an empty slot before K's slot. K is then missed, which is not "found then lost". A mirror slot never goes back to empty, so a later lookup still cannot lose a key it once found. Neither stated rule flags a key that is never found, so two of the four mutations the plan says must fail would pass. D10's purpose is that lookup finds every key the mirror holds live, and that is not checked.
findings.evidence: Plan D10: "That walk would miss keys ... slot i can be delivered empty while K is delivered live further on" and "A mirror slot never goes back to empty". Plan S2: "Mutations that must fail: no repair; headers stored in one pass (no pass B); values after headers; a slot allowed back to empty". The stated rules are only monotonic-found and monotonic-value.
findings.suggested_change: Add a rule: after a reader's acquire of DELIVERIES returns N, every key live in staging N (equally, every key get_next_key returns) is found by lookup with at least the staged value. Check it also mid-delivery for keys whose live header the reader has already acquired. Keep the stagings with gaps and wraparound.

findings.title: S3 cannot apply RULES-round2 as stated: no per-key unstable count, no build for run g, and no new seed per trial

(2) Run g needs wait bound 0. C5 sets it at compile time (WAIT_BOUND_NS), S3 fixes the bound at 100,000 ns in the checked-in PTX, and the extra builds S3 lists are FAULT 1/2/5/6 only. D2 fixes SEED in the layout header and C5's keys are fixed (key_of(j) = 1000 + 7919 j), so all 50 trials see the same slot collisions.

findings.suggested_change: Give the test build a way to report unstable per call: a debug out-parameter or return code under a test define, or per-key counters in the test kernels. Add a BPFTIME_DEVHASH_WAIT_BOUND build for run g. Vary the key set per trial (an offset or multiplier), since the seed is fixed. Or list the RULES checks S3 leaves out.

findings.title: D1, S3 and S6 disagree on who handles "no device copy"
findings.plan_section: D1 (trampoline branches "serve calls the pass does not rewrite (a non-constant fd, or no device copy at patch time)"); S6 ("Base 0: NULL and -1 inline"; mirror of :135); S3 tests ("With no copy (base 0): -1 and NULL")

findings.title: D8: the sealer's INFLIGHT load is acquire, but the store-buffer argument needs seq_cst
findings.plan_section: D8; S2 seal race test
findings.problem: The plan contradicts itself. Line 75 says the sealer "stores PHASE = 1 (seq_cst), then waits ... for INFLIGHT == 0 (acquire)". Line 76 then argues "Store-buffer argument (seq_cst on both sides)". The store-buffer case (sealer reads INFLIGHT 0, writer reads PHASE 0) is ruled out only when the sealer's first INFLIGHT load after its PHASE store is seq_cst, or when a seq_cst fence sits between them. In the C++ model an acquire load is outside the single total order, so both stale reads are allowed. A writer can then insert into the CPU table after the image was built, and the key is silently missing from the device copy. On the current build this does not fire, because the default target emits LDAR. It fires once the build targets the Orin's own core, which has RCpc: there the load becomes LDAPR, which may complete before the earlier STLR. S2's in-process seal-race test runs on the default build, so it cannot expose this.
findings.evidence: Plan line 75: "The sealer stores PHASE = 1 (seq_cst), then waits, bounded at 1 s, for INFLIGHT == 0 (acquire)." Line 76: "Store-buffer argument (seq_cst on both sides)". Compile of the D8 handshake (/tmp/claude-2002/devhash-plan-review/cpu-concurrency/sb.cpp): clang++-16 -O2 -march=armv8-a gives sealer `stlr; ldar`. clang++-16 -march=armv8.2-a+rcpc and g++ -O2 -mcpu=cortex-a78ae both give sealer `stlr x1,[x0]; ldapr x0,[x0]`. In every case the writer is `ldaddal`/`ldar`. /proc/cpuinfo on the board lists `lrcpc ilrcpc`. No -march or -mcpu appears in CMakeLists.txt, cmake/ or runtime/CMakeLists.txt, so the RCpc form is latent, not current.
findings.suggested_change: Write the sealer's first INFLIGHT load as seq_cst, or put std::atomic_thread_fence(seq_cst) between the PHASE store and the wait loop. Later polls may stay acquire. Give the exact memory order of all four operations in D8. Note that S2's seal-race test cannot catch this ordering, and add an asm check (no ldapr between the PHASE store and the first INFLIGHT load) or a code comment that pins the order.

findings.title: Takeover from an owner that died before PHASE 2 seeds from an empty mirror; first copy vs takeover is chosen by pid
findings.plan_section: D7, D9, D11; S4 code (owner CAS, "Takeover uses takeover_image()") and tests
findings.problem: D11 says a process "taking over from a dead owner seeds the fresh block from the mirror". The mirror is filled only just before PHASE = 2 (S4 step 7). Suppose the owner dies after the owner CAS but before PHASE 2: during the up to 1 s seal wait, during iteration, or during the copy (for example the target crashes or is killed at start-up). The next process then finds a dead OWNER_PID with PHASE at 0 or 1. Seeding from the mirror then seeds an empty or partial mirror. Every prefilled key in the CPU table is lost from the device copy, and once PHASE goes to 2 they are also hidden from CPU lookups. With PHASE left at 1, CPU writes stay EPERM forever. The plan never says how a caller decides between seal_and_build_image() and takeover_image(). The existing owner rule cannot decide it either. `while (cur != mine)` treats a process whose pid equals the stored dead pid (pid reuse, or the same pid in a fresh pid namespace) as already the owner, so it never sees a takeover at all. The S4 takeover test covers only a clean exit after a delivery.
findings.evidence: Plan D11 lines 118-119: "A process taking over from a dead owner seeds the fresh block from the mirror". S4 lines 298-305 put the owner CAS first and "7. PHASE = 2 (release), after the mirror holds the seeded image". S4 line 306: "Takeover uses takeover_image()". S4 test line 315: "a forked owner exits after one delivery". nv_gpu_model_maps.cpp:706-721: `uint64_t cur = __atomic_load_n(owner, ...); while (cur != mine) { if (cur != 0 && kill((pid_t)cur, 0) == 0) ... CAS }`. When the stored pid equals getpid(), the loop is skipped and no takeover is detected. The seal runs at agent attach (bpf_attach_ctx.cpp:642-643, inside init_attach_ctx_from_handlers), so an owner killed during start-up is a plain SIGKILL case.
findings.suggested_change: Choose the path by PHASE, not by the owner CAS. PHASE 0: seal. PHASE 1: the previous sealer died; the table is frozen and writers already get EPERM, so reset the mirror to empty and run the seal and image again, without waiting for writers who saw PHASE 1. PHASE 2: takeover_image(). State this in D11 and S4. Add S4 tests: the owner SIGKILLed during the seal wait (PHASE 1 left behind), and between pass B and pass C of a delivery. The next process must keep every prefilled key and every delivered live key.

findings.title: The seal iterates the CPU table through stripe locks that a dead process can hold, so agent attach can hang without bound
findings.plan_section: D8 ("without a lock that a dead process can hold"), D9 ("the agent iterates it")
findings.problem: INFLIGHT counts only updates and deletes. The only iteration that hash_map_impl offers, next_key, spins on stripe locks without a bound. A tool killed inside a get_next_key call during phase 0 leaves its stripe locked while INFLIGHT is 0. The seal's wait then succeeds, and its iteration spins forever on that stripe. The seal runs inside init_attach_ctx_from_handlers, which holds ctx_mutex and the interprocess map_binding_mutex. So the target's agent attach never finishes, and every process that creates or closes a map, or loads a program with bindings, blocks on that mutex. The 1 s bound in D8 does not cover this wait.
findings.evidence: bpftime_hash_map.hpp:784-822: next_key calls `bpftime_spin_lock(&st.lock)` at :791 and :811. CLAUDE.md (Hash Map Concurrency): "A process killed inside a writer leaves its stripe locked (writers of that stripe and `next_key` calls reaching it hang, lookups do not); a tool killed inside `next_key` is such a holder too." Plan D8 line 72 increments INFLIGHT only for CPU writers. bpf_attach_ctx.cpp:192-198 takes ctx_mutex and `map_binding_mutex(*memory)` around instantiation; create_map_basic_info is reached at :642-643. handler_manager.cpp:57, :68 and :118 take the same mutex for handler set and clear.
findings.suggested_change: Once INFLIGHT reads 0 with PHASE at 1, the table has no writers. Iterate its elements without stripe locks, reading each element word and key with acquire as lookups do. Alternatively, try-lock each stripe under the same 1 s deadline and fail closed. Say which in D9. Add an S2 test: a forked process SIGKILLed while holding a stripe lock in next_key (lock_stripe_for_test exists), then the seal ends within its bound.

findings.title: A dead writer leaves INFLIGHT at 1 forever; the S2 kill test's 'later CPU updates work' holds only if the kill lands outside the stripe lock
findings.plan_section: D8 (timeout), D15; S2 seal race test (forked writer SIGKILLed)
findings.problem: After a writer dies inside an operation, INFLIGHT is never decremented. Every later seal by any process, for the life of the segment, waits 1 s and fails, so the map never gets a device copy. The plan says only that the copy "fails closed" and is logged. Failures are not cached: get_gpu_mem_buffer caches only successful copies, and it is called for every map once per CUDA bpf link. So each link pays another 1 s at agent attach, while holding map_binding_mutex (which blocks the loader's map create and close). The block allocated in S4 step 2 must also be freed on this path. The S2 test says the writer is killed "inside an update" and that "later CPU updates work". That is true only when the kill lands between the INFLIGHT increment and the table call. If it lands inside hash_map_impl's update while the stripe lock is held, later writers of that stripe hang, as documented. As written the test has no defined kill point.
findings.evidence: Plan lines 77-79: "On timeout (for example a writer killed inside an operation): PHASE goes back to 0, the copy fails closed ... and it is logged." S2 lines 245-246: "a writer process forked and SIGKILLed inside an update (INFLIGHT left at 1): the seal times out, PHASE returns to 0, and later CPU updates work." nv_gpu_model_maps.cpp:698-702 and :771: only successful copies enter `made`. :760-766: a failure returns 0 uncached. bpf_attach_ctx.cpp:642-643: create_map_basic_info runs for every CUDA link. bpftime_hash_map.hpp:703-704, :720-721, :759-760: writers hold the stripe lock. CLAUDE.md: "A process killed inside a writer leaves its stripe locked".
findings.suggested_change: State that a dead writer disables the device copy for the life of the segment, or make INFLIGHT able to tell a dead writer, for example per-writer slots holding a pid. Record the seal failure per map per process, and do not seal again unless INFLIGHT has changed. Free the step-2 block. In S2, place the kill with a test hook between fetch_add and the table call. Test a kill inside the table separately, as the documented hang of that stripe. Assert that a second seal attempt fails within its bound and that the map stays in phase 0.

findings.title: D15 rollback: 'PHASE goes back to 0' is wrong for a takeover, and a failed first copy leaves a stale seeded mirror
findings.plan_section: D15; S4 steps 6-7 and the failure-injection test
findings.problem: D15 sends PHASE back to 0 on any staging or registration failure. On a takeover PHASE was already 2. Returning it to 0 reopens CPU writes on the long-frozen CPU table and switches CPU lookups back to it, so every delivered key and value disappears from the CPU view. On the first-copy path the mirror may already hold the seeded image when the failure comes, and D10 says a mirror slot never goes back to empty. Phase-0 deletes and inserts then change the table, and a later successful seal places keys anew. The stale mirror headers survive into PHASE 2: a deleted key is found live, and a slot can get a different key, which breaks the invariant. The 1531 structure this builds on also cannot report a registration failure. It pushes the copy into the process cache before registering, and register_device_array returns void, both when there is no staging buffer and when there is no current context. A later call would return the cached, undelivered address.
findings.evidence: Plan D15 lines 158-159: "If the staging allocation or registration fails, get_gpu_mem_buffer returns 0 (no device copy) and PHASE goes back to 0." D10 lines 101-102: "A mirror slot never goes back to empty". S4 line 317 tests only "A failure injected after the seal". nv_gpu_model_maps.cpp:771-773: `made.push_back({ this, d, s }); gpu_model::register_device_array(...)`. :634-641 returns on a staging failure; :654-657 returns on no context. Both return void.
findings.suggested_change: On the first-copy path, reset the mirror to all-empty before storing PHASE = 0. No reader uses it outside phase 2. On a takeover, keep PHASE 2 and the mirror unchanged and only return 0. Make registration return a result, add the copy to the process cache only after it succeeds, and free the block on failure. Tests: a failure injected in a takeover keeps PHASE 2 and lookups unchanged. A failure on the first copy, then a phase-0 delete, then a successful seal: the deleted key is absent from the mirror.

findings.title: S2 mirror test: two of its four mutations cannot fail the stated rules
findings.plan_section: S2 mirror test; D10 passes
findings.problem: The readers only look keys up. The rules are (1) once a reader has found a key live, it finds it on every later lookup, and (2) a found value is never below the staged value. Two of the four mutations can only make a key not found yet; they never make a found key disappear. The first is 'no repair'. Delivery N stages path slot i empty and slot j live K. The mirror keeps i empty, so every lookup of K stops at i and misses until a later delivery fills i. No reader ever finds K and then loses it, so rules 1 and 2 hold. The second is 'headers stored in one pass (no pass B)'. Take home(K) = S-2, i = S-1 and j = 0, with the single pass in slot order, so j is stored before i. A lookup either reads S-1 empty and misses, or reads it non-empty through i's release store, which also makes j's earlier store visible. So it never finds and then loses K. The reader that pass B protects is a slot scan. get_next_key(NULL) acquires live K at slot 0, and an immediate lookup(K) then reads S-1 still empty and returns ENOENT for a key get_next_key just returned. D10's claim that a reader acquiring a live header sees every slot's occupancy is about exactly this reader, and the test has none.
findings.evidence: Plan S2 lines 249-255: readers "look keys up". "Rules: once a reader has found a key live, it finds it on every later lookup; a found value is never below the value staged with that header. Mutations that must fail: no repair; headers stored in one pass (no pass B); values after headers; a slot allowed back to empty." D10 lines 109-110: "A reader that acquires a live header sees ... the occupancy of every slot (pass B)". Code-map risk (delivery reader): "lookup then misses a key that get_next_key returns".
findings.suggested_change: Add two rules and the readers that check them. (a) A publish marker: the writer increments a release counter after each apply_delivery. A reader that acquires marker >= N must find by lookup every key live in staging N; this catches 'no repair'. (b) A scanning reader: for each key that get_next_key returns, an immediate lookup must succeed; with the wraparound stagings this catches 'no pass B'. Keep the existing rules for 'values after headers' and 'back to empty'.

findings.title: The owner rule takes over a live owner on EPERM or across pid namespaces, giving two writers of one mirror
findings.plan_section: D10 ("the delivery thread (the only writer, in the owner process)"), D11
findings.problem: The inherited owner check treats any nonzero result of kill(pid, 0) as a dead owner. That result is EPERM for a live owner under another uid (one target run with sudo, another not), and ESRCH for a live owner in another pid namespace (a container sharing /dev/shm). A second GPU process then takes over a live owner, re-seeds, and both deliver into the same mirror. For 1531 this only flips sums between the two processes. For 1533 it breaks D10. Each device claims new keys independently, so the same empty slot gets K1 in one and K2 in the other. The mirror header then alternates its key (a CPU lookup of K1 finds it, then loses it), and a key's value alternates between two sums and goes down. CLAUDE.md records the same namespace hazard for perf shards, which is why those shards store the pid namespace.
findings.evidence: nv_gpu_model_maps.cpp:710: `if (cur != 0 && kill((pid_t)cur, 0) == 0)`. Otherwise :716 CASes the owner away from a live process. Plan D10 lines 97-98: "the delivery thread (the only writer, in the owner process)". CLAUDE.md (Software Perf Event Output): "A producer in a container sharing `/dev/shm` with the tool used to lose its live, idle shard (tgkill from the host: ESRCH)", and shards record "its producer's pid namespace (inode of `/proc/self/ns/pid`)".
findings.suggested_change: For 1533, treat kill() failing with EPERM as alive. Store the owner's pid-namespace inode beside OWNER_PID, and refuse takeover when the namespaces differ (return 0, logged). Add an S4 test with a stubbed liveness check returning EPERM: the second process must get 0.

findings.title: The 'close while delivering ... run under ASan' mutation cannot fail: map objects live in the boost shm segment
findings.plan_section: S4 tests (pin-list mutation); D12 ("The binding is pinned like the map itself")
findings.problem: Map objects and their buffers are created and destroyed by the boost managed_shared_memory allocator inside the mapped segment. ASan instruments malloc and free only. The repo has no ASan poisoning of the segment, so a delivery writing into a destroyed 1533 object or companion writes mapped, unpoisoned memory and ASan reports nothing. The mutation 'leave 1533 out of the pin list' would therefore pass. The companion's pin is also not assured by existing code. create_map_basic_info pins an ARRAY only when the GPU can reach its values, and never in map-usage-stats builds.
findings.evidence: Plan S4 lines 319-320: "Mutation that must fail: 1533 left out of the pin list, so the 'close while delivering' test sees a freed object (run under ASan)." map_handler.cpp:1622-1628 constructs with `memory.construct<...>(anonymous_instance)`; :1789-1793 frees with `memory.destroy_ptr`. map_handler.cpp:1675-1685 destroys at refcount 1. A grep for asan_poison, ASAN_POISON or __SANITIZE_ADDRESS__ in runtime/, attach/ and vm/ finds nothing. cmake/StandardSettings.cmake:73-76 only adds -fsanitize=address,undefined. bpf_attach_ctx_cuda.cpp:484-505: the ARRAY pin is taken only `if (device != nullptr)`, and the function returns nullptr under BPFTIME_ENABLE_MAP_USAGE_STATS.
findings.suggested_change: Assert the outcome directly. After the tool's close, the 1533 impl's and the companion's refcounts must still be above 0, or a test hook counting destroy_ptr on these objects must read 0. Pin the companion explicitly in get_gpu_mem_buffer under the map_binding_mutex already held there (bpf_attach_ctx.cpp:195-198), whatever the ARRAY path did.

findings.title: CPU readers: no acquire of PHASE or DELIVERIES is specified, and the companion's release has no acquiring reader
findings.plan_section: D7, D9, D10 (CPU lookup), D12 ("then word 0 with release")
findings.problem: D9 stores PHASE = 2 with release after seeding the mirror, but the lookup and get_next_key side never says PHASE is loaded with acquire. The 1533 lookup walks headers with acquire but does not first acquire-load DELIVERIES, as 1531's elem_lookup does. The companion is a plain ARRAY: its lookup returns a pointer and the syscall server copies it with memcpy, so D12's release on word 0 has nothing to pair with. A tool that reads SYNCS_COVERED from the companion and then looks keys up gets no ordering between the two, and the companion's words are not consistent with one another. Through separate bpf() calls the window is tiny, so this is minor, but the plan claims an ordering it does not provide.
findings.evidence: Plan D9 line 88: "The mirror is filled to match before PHASE = 2 is stored (release)." D10 line 94: "A CPU lookup walks from home over `mhdr` with acquire loads". D12 line 143: "The delivery writes words 1-15 relaxed, then word 0 with release." nv_gpu_model_maps.cpp:100-102 (1531): `__atomic_load_n(status_word(GPU_MODEL_STATUS_DELIVERIES), __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE)`. array_map.cpp:35-42 returns `&data[...]` with no atomic. syscall_context.cpp:962-970 does a plain memcpy. nv_gpu_model_maps.hpp:52-54 gives the SYNCS_COVERED contract.
findings.suggested_change: State that every 1533 CPU read path (lookup, get_next_key) first loads PHASE with acquire, then, in phase 2, DELIVERIES from the map object with acquire, as 1531 does. In the README, say that companion words are independent counters read without ordering against one another or against the hash. Drop or qualify the word-0 release claim.

findings.title: The 'opaque resolves in a later delivery' argument holds only for headers published with st.release, not for claiming headers
findings.plan_section: D10 (last argument), D11
findings.problem: Repair applies to every non-empty staged slot that carries a key, including a claiming header. The argument for resolution goes: the walker observed slot i non-empty, then published with release, and the snapshot acquired that header. A claiming header is written by a relaxed compare-and-swap. In PTX the chain may begin with one observation step, after which it must continue through program order or synchronizes-with. Without a release there is no chain from the walker's read of i to the next snapshot. So an opaque slot triggered by a claiming header has no 'next delivery' guarantee; it resolves only after that key is published. If the owner dies or makes its final delivery first, the slot stays opaque, and D11 makes it permanently opaque in the new device.
findings.evidence: Plan lines 111-113: "The device header was non-empty when K's walker passed it, which happened before K's release publish. The next snapshot launch is stream-ordered after the one that acquired K's header." c5-device-part.cu:159 `atom.relaxed.gpu.global.cas.b64` for the claim (:374, :447). st.release is used only in publish (:179, :312) for live and refused. PTX ISA 9.5 chapter 8 text lines 339-360: base causality order needs program order or "X synchronizes with Y"; observation order may be only the first step.
findings.suggested_change: Reword: a repair triggered by a live or refused header resolves in the next delivery; one triggered by a claiming header resolves once that key is published; an opaque slot left at the final delivery or at an owner's death is permanent (D11). Include a claiming-triggered repair that persists over several stagings in the S2 host model.

findings.title: The CPU walk's rule at a non-live slot holding K is unspecified; after a takeover a key can have a stale slot ahead of its new live one
findings.plan_section: D4, D10 (CPU lookup), D11
findings.problem: After a takeover, a claiming or refused K in the mirror becomes opaque in the new device, and D11 allows K to be inserted again. K then takes a slot further along its path while the mirror still shows the old non-live K header. Pass C's store order is unspecified, and with wraparound the new live slot can be stored before the old slot is changed to opaque. If the CPU walk stops at the first slot holding K, as the device walk does under D4, a lookup of K returns NULL while get_next_key returns K. D10 does not say whether the CPU walk stops there.
findings.evidence: Plan D4 line 50: "A device walk matches K only when the state is 1, 2 or 3 and the key field is K." D10 lines 94-95: the walk "stops at empty. It returns `&mval[j]` only for live K." D11 lines 121 and 124-125: "every other non-empty slot (claiming, refused, opaque) becomes opaque"; "a key once refused can be inserted again if there is room". D10 line 107: "store each changed header (release)", with no order given.
findings.suggested_change: Specify that the CPU walk continues past every non-live header and stops only at empty or a live K. Add a post-takeover staging to the S2 mirror test: K's old slot is refused and its new live slot comes earlier in store order.

findings.title: Mirror seeding is ordered after registration, so the seeding thread can race deliveries; 'the only writer' does not hold
findings.plan_section: S4 steps 6-7; D10 ("the only writer")
findings.problem: S4 registers the map for delivery at step 6, then at step 7 requires the mirror to hold the seeded image. If the seeding thread writes the mirror after registration, it races deliveries of this map. Those run on the drain thread, in application threads at synchronization (BPFTIME_GPU_DELIVERY_AT_SYNC=1), or at exit. run_mutex orders deliveries among themselves, but the seeding thread does not take it. D10's argument assumes a single writer.
findings.evidence: Plan S4 lines 303-305: "6. register for delivery (D15); 7. PHASE = 2 (release), after the mirror holds the seeded image". D10 line 97: "the delivery thread (the only writer, in the owner process)". nv_gpu_model_maps.cpp:651 adds the map to the list at registration. :515, :570-573 and :598 take run_mutex for drain, exit and at-sync deliveries. :592-604: at-sync delivery runs in the application's thread.
findings.suggested_change: Write the seeded mirror before step 6 (or under run_mutex), and say so in S4. Reword D10 to "one writer at a time: the seeding before registration, then deliveries under run_mutex".

findings.title: Two 1533 maps can bind the same companion
findings.plan_section: D12 (companion naming and binding)
findings.problem: The rule checks that one hash map finds exactly one companion. It does not check that one companion is claimed by exactly one hash map. Two 1533 maps whose names agree in their first 12 bytes derive the same "_st" name, each finds one match, and both bind it. Their deliveries then overwrite each other's words, alternately under run_mutex when one process owns both, or concurrently when two processes own them.
findings.evidence: Plan D12 lines 131-135: "Its name is the hash map's name truncated to 12 bytes plus `_st` ... It requires exactly one match: none or two means no companion".
findings.suggested_change: While binding (under map_binding_mutex), also count the 1533 maps that derive the same companion name. With more than one, bind none and log it. Add an S4 case with two hash maps sharing a 12-byte prefix.

findings.title: CPU programs writing through 1533 lookup pointers are not covered by the phases
findings.problem: D7 refuses only update and delete. A CPU bpf program (in any agent process) that adds through a lookup result bypasses INFLIGHT and PHASE. With a phase-0 or phase-1 pointer into the CPU table, an add made after the image was built is silently lost. With a phase-2 pointer to `&mval[j]`, the add goes into the mirror, and the next pass A overwrites it, so readers see the value go down. S2's 'never below staged' rule does not cover that case. The plan describes these pointers ("stay valid") without saying that writes through them are outside the contract.
findings.evidence: Plan D9 lines 89-90: "Pointers from phase-0 lookups stay valid ... After the copy they show the sealed value". D10 line 95: returns `&mval[j]`. D10 line 103: "pass A: write changed values". The 1531 equivalent is nv_gpu_model_maps.cpp:111.
findings.suggested_change: In D7 and the S7 README, state that CPU programs must not write through 1533 lookup results: adds after the seal are lost, and in phase 2 the next delivery overwrites them.

findings.title: A get_next_key dump that spans the seal changes order and can skip keys
findings.plan_section: D7, S2 (get_next_key in slot order)
findings.problem: In phases 0 and 1, get_next_key follows the CPU table's bucket order (a seeded hash). In phase 2 it follows mirror slot order (D2's hash). Suppose a dump started before PHASE 2 continues after it with a key it already got. The dump then resumes from that key's mirror slot, and keys earlier in slot order that it has not yet returned are skipped. bpf's htab restarts from the first key only when the key is missing.
findings.evidence: bpftime_hash_map.hpp:780-783: "The key after key in bucket order, chain order within a bucket". The bucket comes from a multiply seeded per map (CLAUDE.md, Hash Map Concurrency). In hack_fatbin the pass runs on the module before the trampoline is prepended (nv_attach_impl.cpp:1224-1228: route, then filter_out_version_headers_ptx(wrap_ptx_with_trampoline(...))). The probe functions sit at the top of the module, ahead of every entry. The by-value dump dumpTVF-lat_mmvq/81ea6349...ptx has the trampoline at lines 1-2538, the probe functions at 2539-3094 and the first .entry at 3095. Text appended to the module therefore follows every call. PTX needs a function declared before a call names it. With no declaration, the routed module does not compile, compile_ptxs throws, and the original image is loaded without probes (CLAUDE.md, 'CUDA Attach: Effects On The Application'). C2's hcall form compiled only because make_hashforms.py:180-185 put __bph_walk before the probe functions. findings.title: The call ABI between the emitter and the clang-made functions is not specified and no test exercises it
findings.plan_section: D1, S3 ("Signatures take (base, key, value pointer, flags), and the geometry as immediates"), S6 constant-fd update and lookup fallback
findings.problem: The emitter has to declare .param types that match clang's output exactly. Clang emits .param .b32 for each u32 argument, .param .b32 func_retval0 for an int return, C++-mangled names for any function not declared extern "C" (the noinline helpers C5 has, such as wait_resolved, become _Z13wait_resolvedyj), and .visible on everything. A width mismatch is a ptxas error, so the module is unprobed. If devhash_insert returns int and the emitter zero-extends into the program's 64-bit r0, then -17 reaches the program as 4294967279: a 'ret == -17' or signed 'ret < 0' test fails silently. The plan fixes neither the return type nor the sign extension. Appended names without a reserved prefix can also collide with a function in the application's own module (duplicate definition). S6's tests are text comparisons, and the only emitted text run on the GPU is the hash. No step runs an emitted insert call.

findings.title: The emitter's header decode and row-to-address formula are a second layout copy that no test checks
findings.plan_section: S1 ("The one place the hash is written a second time, as PTX text, is the emitter"); S6 inline hit path; section 3 row "layout copies disagree | S1, S6 hash-equality test"
findings.problem: The inline hit path writes as PTX text more than the hash. It writes: the header decode (key in bits 63-32, state in bits 2-0, row in bits 31-3); the live test; the sharded address, rows region + (row*shards + shard)*8, for row < R; and the single-word address, single region + (row - R)*8, for row >= R. A runtime branch or select on row < R chooses between the two. S1 supplies the constants, but these operations exist in PTX text only in the emitter. S6 cross-checks only the hash. The whole-block text tests compare the output with strings written by the same author. A wrong shift, mask or region in the emitter would send hits on one path to the wrong words, while devhash_lookup on the other path is correct.

Code map risk: "Layout copies can disagree ... A mismatch gives silent misses or a second slot for one key". The 1531 emitter writes its own shard formula as text (nv_thread_local_routing.cpp:759-801).

Use a directory holding live keys at their home slots with rows below and above R, plus claiming, refused and opaque headers at home. Compare the pointer each lookup returns with devhash_lookup's for the same key, thread and shard. A mutation such as a single-row region off by 8, or row bits shifted by 2, must fail it.

findings.title: The opaque key field is not defined, and the S3 opaque test cannot catch a port that matches on the key alone
findings.plan_section: D4, D11, S3 opaque test
findings.problem: D4 defines opaque as "occupied with no key" and says a walk matches K "only when the state is 1, 2 or 3 and the key field is K". D11 turns refused and claiming slots into opaque but does not say what key field they keep. C5's code matches on the key field first. Its lookup returns NULL at the first slot whose key is K whatever the state. Its insert treats a slot with key K that is neither live nor refused as claiming and waits the full bound, because state 4 never resolves. If a takeover keeps the old key (opaque(K)) and the port keeps C5's test, a refused K can never be inserted again, and a K re-inserted further on is missed by lookups. That contradicts D11's "a key once refused can be inserted again". The S3 opaque test names no mutation and no key field. Seeded with key field 0 and K != 0, as "no key" suggests, the unmodified C5 bodies pass it.

findings.title: D10's "next snapshot sees the slot" follows from chapter 8 only for live and refused headers
findings.plan_section: D10 ("An opaque slot from repair gets its real header in a later delivery ...")
findings.problem: For a live or refused header the chain holds by the text of chapter 8. The walker's read of gap slot i observes a non-empty write W' (8.9.2). That read precedes, in program order, the st.release at slot j. The release synchronizes with snapshot N's ld.acquire (8.9.4). Then come thread end, kernel end, the stream order to snapshot N+1 (8.9.4 API synchronization), and N+1's read of slot i. The causality axiom (8.10.6) then forbids that read from returning the zero. But repair also fires on claiming(K) headers, which are written by the relaxed CAS: that is not a release pattern (8.8), so no synchronizes-with exists. For gaps repaired because of a claiming header, the next snapshot may still read slot i empty. The mirror stays safe, since it keeps opaque, but the sentence claims more than the document gives.

findings.title: After takeover, a full directory with count below max_entries can persist and make every insert of an absent key wait the full bound
findings.plan_section: D4, D11 ("count = L"; "a key once refused can be inserted again if there is room")
findings.problem: Before a takeover, a full directory implies the count is at or will reach max_entries, because count = live + refused slots (every winner adds once). D11 turns refused and claiming slots into opaque without counting them and sets count = L. The device never reclaims an opaque slot. If the mirror had no empty slot and L < max_entries (for example, claims in flight or keys published after the last delivery when the owner died), then every insert of an absent key walks all S slots. It then waits in full_directory for a count that cannot rise, and returns an unstable E2BIG after 100,000 ns requested (up to 89 us elapsed in round two). That includes a refused key D11 says can come back.

findings.suggested_change: State the case in D11 and in the S7 README. Add a takeover_image test with a full mirror and L < max_entries that counts the unstable E2BIGs, so the cost is known.

findings.title: hash_map_desc has no counterpart to sum_has_copy's shard check, which the inline shard mask relies on

verdicts.reason: Holds as a rare edge case. After a takeover, count = L, and opaque slots are never reclaimed. If the mirror has no empty slot and L < max_entries, then no insert can win a CAS, so the count cannot rise. Every insert of an absent key, a once-refused key included, then waits out the full-directory bound and gets an unstable E2BIG. Refused slots exist only once the count reached max_entries, so the case needs rows below max_entries still claiming at the last delivery. That is rare but reachable, and neither D11 nor DESIGN.md states it.
